h: Israel Remains Children While Growing Toward One Heart

p: בָּנִים אַתֶּם לַה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם (דְּבָרִים יד, א)
"You are children of Hashem your God" (Devarim 14:1).
If you conduct yourselves as children,
The matter: one must note in the passage
that at first the entire passage
"and He will give you mercy and multiply you," etc.,
"to do what is right in the eyes of Hashem your God" (Devarim 13:18–19);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ פָּסוּק זֶה בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים
and afterward this pasuk is in the plural:
and afterward it returns to the singular (Devarim 14:2):
"For you are a holy people," etc.,
a mighty one who conquers his inclination;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסִפְרֵי פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ
in the manner of what they said in the Sifrei on this parshah:
"to do what is right in the eyes of Hashem your God,"
in the manner of what they said (Taanis 15a):
'and joy for the upright in heart.'"
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עוֹד עֵסֶק עִם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
who still has dealings with the evil inclination,
a mighty one who conquers his inclination;
that it shine for him so that he can conquer it.
is one who has already merited uprightness of heart,
as it says, "and joy for the upright in heart."
for through the tzaddik's meriting light,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה אַחַר כָּךְ מִמֵּילָא
through this he afterward merits on his own
to straighten the heart as well,
and he merits the aspect of
"and joy for the upright in heart."
And this is what it says:
"to do what is right in the eyes of Hashem your God";
what is right in the eyes of Heaven."
"When you do what is good and right," etc.:
and "right" in the eyes of man;
and here it decides like Rabbi Yishmael,
for it is written, "what is right in the eyes of Hashem your God,"
That is, when one merits straightening the heart
And it is written in the singular,
in the manner of what they said in the holy Zohar
and here, 'I am Hashem your God' (plural),
'Every man shall fear his mother and his father,'" etc.,
לָא אִשְׁתְּכָחוּ קַמֵּי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
"they were not found before the Holy One, blessed be He,
with one heart and one will,
when they stood at Mount Sinai;
everything was said in the singular;
for they were not found so much
it first spoke in the singular.
"You are children of Hashem your God,"
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אִם אֵינָם בְּמַעֲלָה כָּל כָּךְ
that even if they are not on so high a level
as at the Giving of the Torah,
when they were like one man with one heart,
עַל פָּסוּק וַיִּחַן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר (שְׁמוֹת יט, ב)
on the pasuk "and Yisrael encamped," etc. (Shemos 19:2)
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם כֵּן בָּנִים אַתֶּם
And this is what Rabbi Yehudah was precise about:
"If you conduct yourselves as children," etc.;
that is, if they merely conduct themselves
even if they are not actually like children,
who strive like a son who strives
to fulfill his father's desire and will
But if they act corruptly, Heaven forbid,
even if they act corruptly, Heaven forbid,
"you are children of Hashem your God,"
in the Sifrei and in the Gemara (Kiddushin 36a).
this pasuk is said in the plural;
that is, in the end they will rectify everything
"And it shall be, because you listen," etc.,
that the end will be that "you will listen"
and it will enter the heart,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ חוֹזֵר וְאוֹמֵר בִּלְשׁוֹן יָחִיד
And afterward it says again in the singular:
"For you are a holy people," etc.;
for in truth, at the root,
כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד בְּלֵב אֶחָד
all of Yisrael are like one man with one heart,
as they were at the time of the Giving of the Torah;
and so will all of Yisrael merit in the future.
"Who is like Your people Yisrael, one nation" (Shmuel II 7:23).
